newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin embraces Iran as West condemns Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin embraces Iran as West condemns Tehran.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin praised relations with Iran on Friday as Western nations distanced themselves from Tehran after a German court ruled that Iran ordered the 1992 murders of Kurdish activists in Berlin.

"We have good, positive cooperation with Iran, which shows a tendency to grow," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying during talks in the Kremlin with Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, the head of the Iranian parliament.
The Russian president saw a "basis to strengthen and develop these relations". Interfax made no mention of Thursday's court ruling in Germany.

Germany expelled four Iranian diplomats and recalled its ambassador after the court verdict. The European Union has suggested that member countries recall their ambassadors from Iran "for consultations".
Russia, which has expressed an interest in joining the European Union, has been trying to improve relations with Iran.
Nateq-Nouri, addressing the Russian parliament earlier on Frday, also hailed improving relations between Moscow and Tehran. He did not refer to the German court ruling in his address.
